818.t: Switching to electric bass and the jealousy of an old string bass player
818.s: How and why he switched, first seeing electric bass with Freddie Bell, and the Fender he passed up in Las Vegas.
818.q: I switched over to, well, nearly everyone on Bourbon Street at the time, it was playing electric bass, or some people refer to it as guitar bass. So I figured, well, I have to keep up with the times. I'm getting to be an old man now. If I want to keep working, I better switch over. So anyway, I…

818.t: Why Streeman picked him for bass
818.s: He explains Streeman knew he owned a bass and was practicing at home.
818.q: Well, he knew I had a bass at the house that I'd been working out on. Because I told him when I bought the bass, I said, I bought me a string bass, Al. I'm practicing at the house. And I had no idea that the bass player was ever going to quit. And he was a good friend of mine, a fine bass player. I…

798.t: Forced onto bass at a Young Men Olympia funeral
798.s: At a Young Men Olympia funeral with Dominic Remy leading, the hired bass player did not show up, and Clark was made to play the bass. He bought a fingering chart and taught himself.
798.q: You heard of him though, yeah? Well we hired him to play bass. But he didn't have a bass so we got the bass from our bass player which was sick Pete Blanchett. So we brought the bass over to the hall and we waited for him and he didn't come. And it was time to leave. So T-Boy said to me, he says,…

848.t: Switching to bass violin and playing left-handed
848.s: His guitar was stolen during the Depression so he used his father's bass; he restrings it left-handed.
848.q: Yes, I did. It was by force that I had to do so because my guitar was stolen from me. That same guitar that you see over there.

241.t: Butler hears Thomas play and buys a bass
241.s: Butler says Thomas came to Algiers around 1915; he listened under Thomas's house and bought a bass for six dollars down.
241.q: I start with Thomas. When Thomas come here. I didn't go get him. He came here to me. And he came here around in 19 and. Around in 15. And that's when you started. Around in the 1915. September storm. Right about a year after that. I can't remember. Because when this cat come through here with that.…

1024.t: Blisters and buying his own bass on credit
1024.s: Learning through blisters, getting credit at the music store, later bass travels.
1024.ch: Learning bass and Dew Drop days
1024.q: He said, well, what other job you do besides music? I said, well, this is all I do, I got now, the music right now. That's all I do. You don't know how to trust those musicians. You know, that's what he says, you know. I said, well, man, let's, I said, well, let's face it, man. I said, what kind of…

775.t: Switching from trumpet to bass at the Gypsy Tea Room
775.s: He played second trumpet at the Gypsy Tea Room, was asked to learn bass because players were scarce, and from about 1936 played with several bands before Kid Thomas.
775.q: Decatur Street. Uh, we used to wait practically all night. So, about eight till three in the morning, three or four o'clock in the morning. Uh, sometimes five o'clock. Me to play. And, uh, so after that, I got off trumpet. I started playing second trumpet with Rene at the Gypsy Tea Room. We opened…

817.t: Playing a right-handed bass backwards after his grandfather tuned it
817.s: Sherwood explains that his grandfather tuned the borrowed bass for a right-handed player, so he plays it backwards and a left-handed would-be player can use it.
817.q: The show was in the group, it was some insurance company, you know, and they had a little show of their own, I mean, just people who worked for the company, you know, one guy to get up and sing, the other, a couple danced, and some guy, I could hear him talking to the panel, I'd like to play that…

828.t: Borrowing a bass from Dave Poiton for a rehearsal
828.s: Too many trombones in Gus Eli Show's ten-piece band, so Lanoix borrowed a bass for 75 cents and played it for the first time at rehearsal.
828.q: I'll tell you how I happened to change on the bakes. By being in this military band, they had two other fellas which you see on there with trombones. And me, I made the fourth one I believe. They didn't select one of those men on there. There was a boy in there. His name is Gus Eli Show. He's on…

484.t: Playing string bass, and shanghaiing Wingy Manone
484.s: Brownlee swung the string bass until his leg stopped him; he tells how his band picked up Wingy Manone off Canal Street when Emmett Hardy was sick.
484.q: yeah I used to swing it that's yeah I all I quit playing string bass when I got to the part where I couldn't dance with it anymore on account of my bad leg and and I say if you can't dance with it don't play it that is string bass I used to really swing it around what about Winging Manon Winging…

70.t: Playing the two-bass part with Hinton and how he learned bass
70.s: Jackson took over Franz Jackson's two-bass part at the Strand after others failed, having learned bass by watching Billy Taylor, Ysaguirre and Hinton.
70.ch: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
70.q: But, you see, I tell you, Milt, I started to fooling with the bass when Billy Taylor first brought the bass fiddle to McKinney's band.
